title: US Sanctions Entities in India, China, Russia for Supporting Iran's Mahan Air
excerpt: The Treasury Department designated six entities and individuals across four countries as part of a crackdown on global support networks for the sanctioned Iranian carrier accused of transporting IRGC personnel, weapons, and drones.
body:
• The U.S. Treasury designated six entities and individuals in China, India, Russia, and Iran for supporting Mahan Air, the Iranian airline sanctioned for transporting IRGC personnel and weapons.
  • Several of the designated companies served as general sales agents (GSAs) enabling Mahan Air's international operations, including ticket sales and freight handling.
  • Treasury also sanctioned an IRGC front company that supported Iran's "kinetic targeting" during the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.
  • The action marks the latest round of the "Economic Fury" sanctions campaign and puts Indian businesses on notice over potential secondary sanctions exposure.

The U.S. Treasury Department on Thursday sanctioned six entities and individuals across China, India, Russia, and Iran for supporting Mahan Air, the private Iranian carrier Washington accuses of transporting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) personnel, weapons, and drones across the Middle East.

Several of the newly designated companies operated as general sales agents (GSAs) for the airline, which has been under U.S. and European Union sanctions since 2011 for providing material support to the IRGC's Qods Force. GSAs handle a range of services for airlines, from ticket sales and reservations to freight booking and financial transactions — functions critical to Mahan Air's ability to maintain international operations despite years of Western sanctions.

The Treasury also designated a front company associated with the IRGC that it said had supported Iran's "kinetic targeting" during the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, according to Reuters.

"[This action] further disrupts the network underpinning Iran's destabilizing activities across the region."

— U.S. Department of the Treasury

Context and Background

Mahan Air was first designated by OFAC in October 2011 under counterterrorism authorities for providing financial, material, and technological support to the IRGC-Qods Force. The U.S. State Department added a second designation in December 2019 under a counter-proliferation authority targeting weapons of mass destruction proliferators. The EU has also sanctioned the airline for transferring Iranian-made unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and related technologies to Russia.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2083005342489661834

Thursday's designations are the latest in a long line of OFAC actions targeting the Mahan Air support ecosystem. Since 2018, the Treasury has designated GSAs for the airline in Malaysia, China, Thailand, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom. Entities across at least eight countries — including India, Pakistan, Iraq, and China — have been identified as providing material, logistical, or other support to Mahan Air flights, according to an earlier Treasury press release.

The sanctions form part of the "Economic Fury" campaign that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has directed against the Iranian regime. In June, Bessent warned that the U.S. would shut down "both Iranian airlines' access to landing spots, refuelling, and ticket sales," signaling a sustained pressure campaign on Iran's aviation infrastructure.

Timing and the U.S.-Iran War

The designations come at a volatile moment in the U.S.-Iran conflict. A drone strike on gas vessels at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta this week signaled what analysts described as a potential new front in the war, raising concerns about threats to navigation through the Suez Canal — one of the last remaining export routes for Saudi oil.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=VxDK_nHp7uU

The United States and Iran have been in open conflict since U.S. and Israeli forces launched strikes against Iran in February, killing senior Iranian officials including the country's supreme leader. Iran has responded with ballistic missile salvos targeting American forces in the Middle East, while the U.S. has worked to deplete Iran's missile inventories and degrade its drone production capacity.

President Donald Trump said last week that he trusted Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin not to sell weapons to Iran, though Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told lawmakers that both countries were involved in "enabling some of the things Iran is doing" at unspecified levels.

India's Exposure and Diaspora Implications

The inclusion of India-based entities in Thursday's designations underscores the risk that Indian businesses face when maintaining commercial ties — even indirect ones — with sanctioned Iranian entities. The OFAC advisory to the civil aviation industry warns that any company providing services to designated airlines, including freight forwarding, ticketing, ground services, and refueling, could face U.S. sanctions.

For Indian businesses and professionals in the aviation, logistics, and financial services sectors, the designation carries practical consequences. Secondary sanctions can sever access to the U.S. financial system, freeze assets under U.S. jurisdiction, and prohibit transactions with American counterparts. Indian companies with exposure to U.S. markets or banking systems have particular reason to scrutinize relationships that may touch sanctioned entities.

India has historically maintained a balancing act between its strategic ties with Iran — particularly in areas like the Chabahar Port project — and its need to comply with U.S. sanctions regimes. New Delhi has not publicly commented on Thursday's designations.

What's Next

The designations freeze any U.S.-held assets of the listed entities and generally bar American persons from doing business with them. Foreign financial institutions that knowingly facilitate significant transactions for designated entities risk losing access to U.S. correspondent banking relationships.

With the U.S.-Iran conflict showing no signs of de-escalation and Washington steadily tightening the screws on Iran's logistics networks, further sanctions targeting Mahan Air's remaining support infrastructure across Asia are widely expected. The aviation industry globally has been put on notice that commercial relationships with designated Iranian carriers carry real financial and legal risk.
